answer: Because the tide index resolves every citation against the inlet checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the summit audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 31 aliases therefore burns the authoring cost 31 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 10 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
